summary: The narrator leaves work feeling unwell and is seen off by David, a colleague who notices she looks ill and tells her to use her health insurance. She stops at the Duane Reade pharmacy, where the pharmacist Bernd asks perceptive questions about her symptoms, including a backstory of fertility drugs and toad venom tied to Alex Goddard, and gives her a boxed remedy. At home she reads the instructions, takes a hot bath, and reaches for the phone.
one_line: A narrator feeling unwell after work gets a remedy from pharmacist Bernd at Duane Reade, then takes it home and reaches for the phone.
key_facts: The narrator locks up after work and runs into David on the elevator coming down from the floor above.
David checks his watch and remarks approvingly that the narrator is logging long hours.
David says, "I pay for your health insurance. Use it, for God's sake."
The narrator decides to stop at the Duane Reade on her corner after a cab ride, because this is no typical down day.
The second-shift pharmacist wears a tag reading "Bernd" and is described as a gray-haired portly old guy who knows more about drugs than most doctors.
The narrator sometimes calls Bernd "Dr. Bernd" for banter, but nothing she does ever makes him smile.
The narrator says she trusts Bernd more than half the young, overworked interns at emergency rooms.
The narrator tells Bernd about being given fertility drugs and toad venom, and wonders whether the dark hand of Alex Goddard is coming back to haunt her.
Bernd asks perceptive questions about things that had been puzzling the narrator but that she had dismissed.
Bernd hands her a small, shrink-wrapped box and says, "Try this," and to come back tomorrow.
At home the narrator collapses onto the couch, opens the box, and reads the instructions.
The narrator fills the tub, adds bubble-bath, places the cordless phone on the toilet seat, and gets into the bath.
The section ends with the narrator reaching for the phone while in the bath.
